began in 2013 when Warren Buffett teamed up with the Brazilian private equity firm 3G Capital to take H.J. Heinz private in a $23B deal. Two years later, in July 2015, Berkshire and 3G orchestrated a massive blockbuster merger between Heinz and Kraft Foods Group to create The Kraft Heinz Company
Initially, the investment looked like a classic Buffett triumph, with Kraft Heinz

shares climbing above $90 in early 2017 and valuing Berkshire's stake at nearly $30 billion. However, the partnership soon soured as 3G Capital's aggressive zero-based budgeting and cost-cutting strategies starved the company's legacy brands of marketing and innovation just as consumer tastes shifted toward healthier, fresher foods. While 3G Capital quietly exited its entire stake by early 2024, Berkshire (BRK.A) (BRK.B) continued to hold on through accounting restatements, leadership overhauls, and Kraft Heinz's aborted late plan in 2025 to split itself into two separate companies.
